sources.title: m1_walks.py: brute-force walk enumeration against matrix powers
sources.venue: Script written by module m1 in this run
sources.notes: Run with python3 -I; output saved in scripts/m1_walks_output.txt. Enumerates every vertex sequence of length k+1 and compares the count with the matrix power for the board matrix (k = 0..4) and for 200 random simple graphs on 2..6 vertices (k = 0..4). A check, not a proof.

claims.text: N1. Setting: a finite simple undirected graph G = (V, E) with V = {n_1, ..., n_N}; its adjacency matrix A has A_ij = 1 if n_i n_j is an edge and 0 otherwise, so A is symmetric with zero diagonal. The textbook writes v_i and a_ij; the board writes n_i and A_ij. The choice of n_i, and of E for the edge set the board calls V, is the paper's convention.

support.locator: printed p. 11, after Definition 1.1.6 (viewed as page image)
support.quote: A(G) մատրիցը կանվանենք G գրաֆի հարևանության մատրից: Նկատենք, որ ցանկացած i-ի համար (1 ≤ i ≤ n) a_ii = 0, և ցանկացած i, j-ի համար (1 ≤ i, j ≤ n) a_ij = a_ji:
A simple undirected graph G = (V, E) consists of a non-empty set V of vertices and a set E of unordered pairs of distinct elements of V, called edges.

claims.text: N2/N3. In a simple graph there is at most one edge between two vertices, so a walk is determined by its vertex sequence (v_0, ..., v_k) with consecutive vertices adjacent; this is the textbook's Definition 1.2.10 restated, and it is Grinberg's Definition 2.9.1(a). The reversal of a walk is a walk (adjacency is symmetric), and the reversal of a path is a path, so a path from n_i to n_j gives one from n_j to n_i.

support.locator: Definition 1.2.10, printed p. 21 (viewed as page image)
support.quote: Սահմանում 1.2.10: G գրաֆի u0, u1, …, uk-1, uk գագաթներից և e1, …, ek կողերից կազմված u0, e1, u1, …, uk-1, ek, uk հաջորդականությունը կանվանենք k երկարությամբ u0-ից uk շրջանցում կամ k երկարությամբ (u0, uk)-շրջանցում, եթե ei = ui-1ui, երբ 1 ≤ i ≤ k:
A walk (in G) means a finite sequence (v0 , v1 , . . . , vk ) of vertices of G (with k ≥ 0) such that all of v0 v1 , v1 v2 , v2 v3 , . . . , vk−1 vk are edges of G.

claims.derivation: modules/m1.md section 3, remark after Definition 2 and section 3 on N3

claims.text: N5. For every integer k >= 0 the entry (A^k)_ij equals the number of walks of length k from n_i to n_j (A^0 = I). Proof by induction on k, with the walks of length k+1 sorted by their last-but-one vertex. Stated for k >= 1 in Galway Theorem 1.1.3; the case k = 0 is added here.

support.locator: Theorem 1.1.3, printed p. 4 (re-opened and text-checked by m1)
support.quote: Then the entry in the (i, j)-position of the matrix Ak is the number of walks of length k from vi to vj in G.
Random graphs: theorem verified in 1000 (graph, k) cases, no failure

claims.derivation: modules/m1.md section 3 (Theorem 1 and its proof); numerical check in scripts/m1_walks.py

claims.text: N4. Connected in the paper's sense (for all n_i, n_j there is a path, no repeated vertex, from n_i to n_j) is equivalent to the textbook's Definition 2.1.1 read with the textbook's own path of Definition 1.2.12 (a walk with pairwise distinct edges). Direction 1: in a simple graph a walk with distinct vertices has distinct edges. Direction 2: a textbook path is a walk, and a walk from n_i to n_j contains a path from n_i to n_j (statement N6, proved by module m2).

support.locator: Definition 2.1.1, printed p. 48 (viewed as page image)
support.quote: Սահմանում 2.1.1: G գրաֆը կանվանենք կապակցված, եթե նրա ցանկացած երկու u և v գագաթների համար G գրաֆում գոյություն ունի (u, v)-ճանապարհ:

support.quote: Սահմանում 1.2.12: G գրաֆի (u0, uk)-շրջանցումը կանվանենք u0-ից uk ճանապարհ կամ (u0, uk)-ճանապարհ, եթե u0u1-ը,…, uk-1uk-ն G գրաֆի զույգ առ զույգ տարբեր կողեր են:

support.quote: Սահմանում 1.2.13: G գրաֆի (u0, uk)-ճանապարհը կանվանենք պարզ (u0, uk)-ճանապարհ, եթե նրա մեջ մտնող բոլոր գագաթները զույգ առ զույգ տարբեր են:

support.locator: Corollary 2.9.7, p. 39 (premise N6, taken from the evidence file, not re-opened by m1)
support.quote: Then, there is a path from u to v of length ≤ k.

claims.derivation: modules/m1.md section 3, Proposition 1; script check of direction 1 in scripts/m1_walks.py (last line of output)

claims.text: N5. On the board's graph (A with rows 0 1 0 / 1 0 1 / 0 1 0, edges n_1n_2 and n_2n_3) A^2 has rows 1 0 1 / 0 2 0 / 1 0 1. The entry (A^2)_11 = 1 counts the single walk n_1, n_2, n_1, which repeats n_1 and so is not a path; (A^2)_22 = 2 counts n_2, n_1, n_2 and n_2, n_3, n_2, neither a path; (A^2)_13 = 1 counts n_1, n_2, n_3, which is a path. This is the derivation that claim C22 awaited.

support.locator: 3 by 3 grid labelled 'adj.' (viewed as image: rows 0 1 0 / 1 0 1 / 0 1 0)
scripts/m1_walks_output.txt, walks of length 2 from n1 to n1

claims.text: O2 (optional). For i different from j in a graph where n_j is reachable from n_i, the least k >= 1 with (A^k)_ij > 0 is the least length of a walk from n_i to n_j, which by N6 is the least length of a path, and equals the textbook's distance (Definition 1.2.16, which uses shortest textbook paths, i.e. shortest trails, of the same least length). Paramadevan and Sotheeswaran state it as their Theorem 3.

support.locator: Definition 1.2.16, printed p. 22 (viewed as page image)
support.quote: Սահմանում 1.2.16: G գրաֆում u և v գագաթների միջև հեռավորությունը կսահմանենք որպես կարճագույն (u, v)-ճանապարհի երկարություն, եթե G գրաֆում գոյություն ունի առնվազն մեկ (u, v)-ճանապարհ
The distance between two vertices vi and vj is equal to l if and only if l is the smallest integer such that (A_G^l)_ij ≠ 0.

claims.text: N2. The textbook, in the sentence that follows Definition 1.2.10 on printed p. 21 (it is a separate sentence after the definition, not part of its numbered statement), says a walk is abbreviated by the sequence of its vertices u_0, u_1, ..., u_(k-1), u_k, on the understanding that each next vertex is adjacent to the previous one. English rendering: 'We will write a defined (u_0, u_k)-walk briefly as the sequence of its vertices u_0, ..., u_k, assuming that each subsequent vertex is adjacent to the preceding one.'

support.locator: printed p. 21, sentence immediately after Definition 1.2.10 (viewed as page image, PDF p. 22)
support.quote: Սահմանված (u0, uk)-շրջանցումը կրճատ կնշանակենք նրա գագաթների u0, u1, …, uk-1, uk հաջորդականությամբ, ենթադրելով, որ յուրաքանչյուր հաջորդ գագաթ հարևան է նախորդին:

contradictions.summary: Textbook Definition 2.1.1 uses the textbook's path (trail, Definition 1.2.12); the paper's path is Definition 1.2.13 (no repeated vertex).
contradictions.resolution: Settled in m1-4: the two readings of connected agree, by Proposition 1 in modules/m1.md. Direction 2 uses N6 from module m2.
